Definition: a primary particle of conditionality; if, whether, that, etc.:--forasmuch as, if, that, (al-)though, whether. Often used in connection or composition with other particles, especially as in G1489, G1490, G1499, G1508, G1509, G1512, G1513, G1536, G1537. See also G1437.
BiblicalUsage: If is the hinge of the New Testament, the little word that turns a promise into a condition and a warning into a choice. Paul says if any man's work abides, he shall receive a reward, and if a brother is grieved by what we eat, we are no longer walking in love. Titus must be blameless if he is to serve as an elder, and every if in Scripture asks the reader to decide.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's ifs are not traps but invitations, because He sets the condition plainly and then waits for our answer. My position is that faith is saying yes to His if before I see the whole road.
